steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: There you are, Captain! Here, take a look at this blueprint. Occ has been saying it's pointless to design a new electrical transmission distribution valve.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: But more and more big guys are gonna roll out from our factory to the other plates of Londinium!

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: I say we ought to make preparations ahead of time.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: I don't want to hear people complain when they find that these things don't have enough power and torque—

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: 'Those short-sighted idiots!'

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Stop calling me captain. This is a factory; we're not in the Self-Salvation Corps anymore.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Besides, I'm sure Occ has thought about it too. It's just about saving costs where you can.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: I know, I know... but it's the young ones coming after us who would have to deal with any problems.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: I know how you feel, Martin.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: But we have to take things one at a time. Closure shared a bunch of drone technology with us that I would love to put into our new four-legged crawler.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: But problems like power supply and automation don't just solve themselves. It's all good to have them in the blueprints, but let's take one step at a time, starting with the present.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Let's do it Occ's way for now and get a basic version out to meet our present needs.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: File your blueprint with the Londinium Industry Development Association. Don't lose it.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Its mission is to restore Victoria's technological superiority, with the support of Parliament. New ideas should be respected.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: Whatever you say. You're a consultant for them, after all.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: There have been so many new ideas lately that it's getting hard to keep up.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: People are enthusiastic. They can feel that things are changing because of their ideas.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Yes. Factory production lines, a railway system that links all the districts, and walls and artillery that protect all of Londinium.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: We can build them the way we want, with our own two hands.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: I could agree with everything else, but please, not the way you want, Feist, or we're all gonna end up in one big amusement park, where the only form of transportation is ziplines.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Come on, that's just the one that drew the most laughs amongst the proposals that got shot down. Not all of my ideas are like that.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: By the way, are you sure your factory wants to keep Occ in the core workshop? I heard he didn't get along with you at the old place.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Each factory has its own technical secrets, and there's been friction over competition for orders...

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: Well, that's true. Not all of our workers were in the Self-Salvation Corps.

steps.name: Enthusiastic Worker
steps.text: But if Catherine could convince the other factories to join the association and share technologies, then there's nothing for us to hide—

steps.name: Anxious Worker
steps.text: Somebody! Help!

steps.name: Anxious Worker
steps.text: Matthew just got pummeled!

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Have we met before, sir?

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: Not exactly, Madam Speaker.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: The name's Matthew, a humble businessman who owns a little factory. I simply felt the need to speak up about the present situation.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You can write to Parliament, or seek assistance from the Industry Development Association. I have... other things that require my attention.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: I have written to Parliament on behalf of a dozen factories that were shut down. My letter's gone unread for the better part of a month.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: It was the decision of Parliament to shut down a number of factories. You know better than I the state of Londinium's logistics.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: The burden of one factory's debt can crush hundreds of families in Sudean or Highbury.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: We're just asking for the scales to be tipped a little towards us—even if only in a private manner.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: Workers from factories that have been shut down could not even afford to buy medicine on the black market. An experienced line worker is worth ten pieces of machinery.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: I believe in my workers. There is much that they can still do for the city.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: Meanwhile, invaluable Oripathy suppressants are being wasted on dying soldiers on their beds in the Sanatorium.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: What are you on about?!

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: Explaining the realities of economic—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You bloody—
Vina's fist found the man's nose before she knew it.
The man by the name of Matthew grabs his bleeding nose with one hand and searches haplessly for a handkerchief with the other.
Blood continues to seep from the gaps in his fingers, dyeing his clothes red.
More and more onlookers gather, all of them staring at Vina.
There is no hostility or anger in their eyes, but each and every gaze reminds her of her helplessness, of her ill-timing.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I—

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: I understand why you're angry, Madam Speaker. I know... but someone has to say it.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: I assure you it gives me no pleasure.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: I was part of the Self-Salvation Corps that stayed in the city. You came with the Cautus girl, and then you left.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: When the Exemplars came, and I learned from Catherine that you're their leader, I agreed to turn on the boilers to welcome you without a second thought.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: But I didn't recognize you when I saw you standing in the middle of the street, dressed like a king, promising a better life for everyone on behalf of Parliament.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: You knew that some promises could never be fulfilled. You chose to sacrifice some people to save others, didn't you?
She wants to shut him up.
She grabs the man by the collar and lifts him off the ground, but she can see his eyes, and the eyes of everyone standing around.
'Siege solves problems with her fists.'
She wishes she could make these problems go away with her fists, the way she used to.
Something falls out of her pocket and makes a clanging sound on the ground. It has been a long time since she had candy. She forgot the box was in her pocket.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: We believed in you when we agreed to shut down and relinquish our Originium fuel. But now, we can only hope that we're not the ones being marked for sacrifice.

steps.name: Downtrodden Man
steps.text: Not all problems can be solved by your fists... Siege.

spans.text: Not all problems can be solved by your fists...

steps.text: Vina!

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Let Matthew go. Please.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: ...Matthew's views don't represent those of all the workers.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Neither do mine, of course.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: All I know is that a few friends have reached out to Rhodes Island through me, hoping to improve the state of equipment at the Sanatorium. We can't make new equipment appear out of thin air, but maybe we can make the existing kit more efficient.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Most workers still support the current medical system, I think.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No, you don't have to explain, Feist. I was the one who let the blood get to my head.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: You have done as much as you could possibly do.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Improved medical equipment effectiveness, reopening the fast transport tunnels, the central heating system under experimentation... a lot of people have benefited from the changes in a short period of time.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: It's all thanks to how you've given us the green light and fended off trouble for us in Parliament.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: That's my job. How is Catherine?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Granny?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Well... I doubt she would answer, even if I asked. She won't even let people see her cough.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Otherwise, she's the same. Still busy, even though she's not working at the factory anymore. I rarely get to see her.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I had a conversation with her like this last month. She sat on this very chair, and turned down my invitation for her to become a Member of Parliament.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The secret workshop that you kept hidden from the Sarkaz, and the weapon inside—

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Londinium doesn't need it anymore.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Yes, I have reached a consensus with Catherine on this matter.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: As long as you and Catherine are able to unite most of the workers, it's not a bad thing for the weapon to stay under your watch.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Parliament needs oversight. So do I.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The system of Parliament is yet immature. We're still searching, and there are people trying to get something done through it.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But sooner or later, they must understand that the Parliament which revolved around the king is long gone.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Was it when the king was—er—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: No... nothing changed with Parliament when he was hanged, other than power being transferred from the king to the dukes.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: It was only recently that the surviving fellows of the Royal Academy of Sciences were able to resume work on the chronicle of Londinium—

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: A million words that took half a lifetime to compile and edit, encompassing every aspect of Londinium.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I never thought I would get to know my own home again from this angle.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: It was only after reading it that I realized the city's resistance began a long time ago.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: 'When the Sarkaz gained control of the city, it was the Londiniers who still lived within who had, of their own accord, come together to maintain the city's core functions, irrespective of upbringing and status.'

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The Academy's fellows see it as the precursor to the new Parliament.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Seems a little... far-fetched? But it does make sense, in a way.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: But I see another side, Feist. During the war, we were able to set aside our differences, our own interests, in our struggle to survive...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Now, though, I'm not sure.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: There are times that I can't even guarantee my own reason. I need someone to pull me back when I—

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: You want it to be us?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: That was my promise with Catherine. It was you lot who gave me my sword, after all.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The war destroyed many things. Londinium needs your help in order to not fall behind the changing times.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Some of your ideas may create headaches in Parliament and the Royal Academy of Sciences, but that's not such a bad thing.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Hehe.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: A city defense system that belongs only to us, automation that the dukes have long ignored, and a new deterrent for a post-Steam Knight era...

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: Your help is needed in all of this. And it must be for Londinium, not for any individual.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I don't deserve your trust, Feist, and neither does Parliament in its current state... send Matthew my apologies again, if you see him.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: I will continue to lobby Parliament for policies that will improve the condition of workers.

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: The medicine that we purchased from the dukes is on its way. Things will get better, once supply routes are secured.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Hah, who dares threaten the dukes' cargo ships?

steps.name: Vina
steps.text: ...I'll continue to communicate with the ducal representatives in the city.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: We're here for you if you need any help.
Feist stands up, but then hesitates. He does not leave the room.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Granny always scolded me for my fancies.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: But she said nothing the day I brought back the proposals for the future from the Industry Development Association.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: She retired from the line soon after, claiming health issues.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: We like to dream about the future, Vina. We'll pull through.
The office falls quiet. Vina stares at the mountain of papers on her desk, then turns on the radio.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: *Bzzt*—

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Late afternoon today, citizens witnessed the Speaker of Parliament, Alexandrina Victoria, put a scoundrel in his place.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: It was reported that a gentleman had attempted to bribe the Speaker for his own selfish interests, which the Speaker rejected in the most direct manner possible.

steps.name: Radio
steps.text: Many citizens speak highly of Speaker Victoria's charisma and believe that she—

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I guess we've finally learned to trust each other a little bit.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Whether you're confident that this supply route is safe enough for one person to manage... or that most of you have left Victoria, just as you said.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Some sign of trust when you have your little trinket in plain sight.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: This is a city full of homeless, desperate people. Who knows if somebody won't get ideas?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Never said you're not part of the threat, of course.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Not that many people in Londinium remember Reunion's past.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Go ahead, check. Everything on the list is here, and I'll deliver the next batch of medicine on time.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You said most of you have left. What about Nine?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Left. Along with many people for whom there is no place in the city.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Our factories outside the city won't be affected, of course. And the routes you found for us will continue to be useful.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You're not going with them? Londinium isn't a great place for Infected anymore.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: 'Isn't a great place.' Spoken with true Londinier irony.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: When I was little, I was fascinated by the Londinium in the storybooks. The palaces and the gardens where the king and the young princess lived, the adventures to be found in the maze-like factories.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Now I find that Londinium is no different from anywhere else in Victoria. It's no place to make a home.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I stay because somebody has to, and I like doing good, honest work. Besides, the treatment of the Infected in Londinium today is... not terrible.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Really?

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I followed them because they saved my life. I'm not like those who are ready to die, who've already figured out how to die for something worthwhile.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: Besides, in the end, it usually isn't worthwhile. Nobody deserves to die.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: You saved a lot of lives. Thank you, on behalf of the workers.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Stop by Highbury the next time you're passing out pamphlets in the city. I'll see right through that disguise.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: The goods check out. I'm off, then.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: One more thing, Catherine...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: ...If the rocks hurt at night, I know a few techniques to make you feel better.

steps.name: Percival
steps.text: I think you know... our medicine doesn't work as well as the stuff from the big pharmas.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Yes. It may fool the other workers, but it can't fool me. Same for most of the suppressants you can get in Londinium right now.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: At my age, though, I don't have too many lucid days ahead of me. And I guess you could say I've seen worse.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: One more day with my senses is one more thing I can do. That's plenty.

steps.name: Victorian Sergeant
steps.text: Our men have tracked down Reunion's hideouts outside the city, two major factories, and their supply routes.

steps.name: Victorian Sergeant
steps.text: Should we shut them down?

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: No need. Based on available information, they are not a threat to the citizens of Londinium.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: Vina says she has personal reasons to be wary of Reunion.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: But even she admits that they were a big help to us when they incited the citizens to oppose the dukes.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: As for the gray market... just make sure we keep track of everything that's going on. Percival is not stupid. She knows what she's not supposed to touch.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: The Reunion threat is much diminished now that their main members have left Londinium. Continue to monitor the situation.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I will even go so far as to say that establishing contact at a private level is an option, if there is consensus about improving the Infected situation.

steps.name: Victorian Sergeant
steps.text: Understood. We will continue to monitor Reunion activity without taking direct action.

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: I suppose I'm wasting you lot on this kind of work.

steps.name: Victorian Sergeant
steps.text: Of course not, Lady Delphine!

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: From the day we left the Duke of Windermere's ship, to setting intelligence work aside to focus on the assault of Londinium, and now...

steps.name: Delphine
steps.text: ...Do you miss the waters of Lynncardine?
